Equipment safety | Follow safety procedures around pedestrian-vehicle separation, loading docks, and conveyors; clerk status does not imply forklift permission.

Responsibility boundaries | Inventory adjustments, damaged-goods release, expense approval, and equipment operation each have authorization requirements independent of job titles.

Clerks entering warehouses, drivers, and supervisors
Forklifts and material equipment may strike pedestrians, with blind spots and shipping pressure increasing danger.

items.title: What do employers usually look for when hiring?

values: Materials and setup | All data are fictional, paper only
You record receipts and stocktakes in a fictional warehouse. All units are items; carton-to-item relationships follow exercise settings only, and no figures represent actual inventory.
A1 | SKU-A order: 10 cartons of 12 items, expected total 120 items; actual arrival: 9 cartons of 12 items, total 108 items.

A2 | Of the 108 SKU-A items, 5 have visible damage and the remaining 103 appear intact; damaged items remain part of actual receipts, so do not subtract them again from 108 and call that the received quantity.
A3 | SKU-B order: 50 items, with 50 received, but label batches differ from the order; without quality confirmation, matching quantities cannot be marked released.

A4 | Independent SKU-C stocktake: book quantity 80 items, first physical count 78; no cause or other movement evidence is provided. Mark the difference and list recounting and evidence checks as pending without guessing causes.

A5 | Clerks only record and report; warehouse supervisors handle recount checks, quality supervisors decide damage and batch status, and inventory owners handle adjustments through approval workflows. Without approval, do not mark adjusted or available.
Task and outputs
Deliver a receiving table: SKU, unit, expected, received, shortage, visibly intact, damaged, batch status, and source material identifiers.
Also deliver a SKU-C stocktake discrepancy table and one-page handoff: known facts, unconfirmed items, recipients, and next steps; do not write to actual systems.
Reference answer | Complete independently first
SKU-A expected 10×12=120 items, received 9×12=108 items, shortage 120−108=12 items; damaged 5 items, visibly intact 108−5=103 items. Separate shortage and damage columns; actual receipts remain 108.
SKU-B quantity difference 50−50=0 items, with batch mismatch awaiting quality confirmation; matching quantities do not automatically authorize release.

SKU-C physical count−book quantity=78−80=−2 items; cause unknown, so recount and check movement evidence before submission. Hand over separately to supervisors, quality, and inventory owners without substituting for approval.

description.text: What shipping, receiving, and inventory clerks do, how to enter, work risks, and development directions. Based on this occupation's local evidence package and official sources, retaining statistical definitions and data gaps.

subject.name: Shipping, Receiving, and Inventory Clerks
subject.summary: Shipping, receiving, and inventory clerks compare incoming and outgoing goods with orders, shipping manifests, and system records, record quantities, storage locations, damage, and discrepancies, prepare shipping documents, and contact carriers. Work involves data and handoffs and may include warehouse floor duties; inventory adjustments, quality release, and forklift operation each require authorization, and clerical positions are not equivalent to purchasing managers or logistics analysts.
